name: UCI Phishing ML Benchmark
description: Benchmarking Supervised and Unsupervised Machine Learning for Phishing Website Detection Reproducible supervised and unsupervised machine-learning benchmark on the UCI Phishing Websites dataset (ID 327, DOI 10.24432/C51W2X). This is not a production phishing detector: it does not accept raw URLs or live webpages and does not perform URL/webpage feature extraction. All experiments operate on the dataset's 30 pre-engineered, historical attributes. The benchmark compares a majority-prior Dummy baseline against Random Forest, XGBoost, SVM, and MLP classifiers under a stratified 80/20 train/test split, with hyperparameter selection via RandomizedSearchCV on the training partition only, a post-selection cross-validation diagnostic, held-out test evaluation, percentile bootstrap confidence intervals on fixed held-out predictions, and permutation importance for feature contribution. It complements the supervised benchmark with an exploratory unsupervised analysis using PCA, k-Means, and DBSCAN, evaluated against the known labels only as a post-hoc, non-selection diagnostic using Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) and Normalized Mutual Information (NMI). In the archived full-profile run, XGBoost obtained the highest held-out F1 score (0.9734), closely followed by Random Forest (0.9707). The unsupervised analysis showed weak alignment between cluster structure and the known labels, supporting its role as an exploratory complement rather than a substitute for supervised classification.
